summary: A Waybar module that shows the current network download rate in kilobytes per second, refreshed every 2 seconds, and opens a desktop notification with the total data received since the module started when clicked.
targetUsers: Waybar users who want a live download-rate readout in their status bar
Users who want a quick total of data received since the module started
goals: Show the current network download rate in kB/s in the Waybar module label
Refresh the measured rate every 2 seconds
Show the total data received since the module started in a desktop notification on click
nonGoals: Showing upload rate, latency, or per-interface breakdowns
Keeping history of past rates beyond the current reading and the running total
Detecting or resetting the total when the calendar day changes

features.name: Download rate label
features.userOutcome: The user sees the current download rate in kB/s in the Waybar module label.
features.trigger: The module command re-reads the cached label; the service loop refreshes the measurement every 2 seconds.
features.behavior: Each refresh reads the cumulative network-received byte counter, computes the rate as the counter change times 8 divided by the elapsed seconds since the stored sample, converts it to kB/s (1 kB = 1000 B), and writes the cache label with the number scaled to kB/s and 1 decimal. The label is composed as '{value} kB/s'. The first refresh after the service loop starts, or after the stored sample time is more than twice the refresh interval old, stores the new counter and sample time and writes the label with 0.0 kB/s. The module command with no action or --once never measures and only re-reads the cached label. The cache is written as soon as the fetch succeeds; the bar shows it at its next fragment re-run.
features.failureOutcome: When the counter cannot be read, the cache keeps the last good label text with class stale, and the module output rendered from that cache is that text with STALE_SUFFIX appended and class stale; no stored record changes. With no reading ever stored, the label is --.
acceptanceSignals: A refresh with a counter change of 6,250,000 bytes over 5 seconds writes the label '10.0 kB/s' with class normal.
A refresh with a counter change of 500,000 bytes over 5 seconds writes the label '100.0 kB/s' with class normal.
The module command with no action renders the cached label text without measuring the counter.
After a failed refresh the module output is the last good label text with STALE_SUFFIX appended and class stale.
With no stored reading the module output is '--' with class empty.

features.name: Total received notification
features.userOutcome: The user clicks the module and gets a desktop notification with the total data received since the module started.
features.trigger: A click on the Waybar module.
features.behavior: The click reads the stored rate sample record and sends a desktop notification whose body states the total data received since the module started, formatted with the largest SI unit whose value is at least 1 and 2 decimals (plain B below 1000). The total is the stored cumulative received counter minus the counter stored when the service loop started. With no stored record the click sends nothing and exits non-zero.
features.failureOutcome: With no stored record the click sends no notification and exits non-zero; a failed notification request makes the command exit non-zero.
acceptanceSignals: A click with a stored record whose total received is 3,670,016,000 bytes sends a notification whose body contains '3.67 GB'.
A click with a stored record whose total received is 999 bytes sends a notification whose body contains '999 B'.
A click with no stored record sends no notification and exits non-zero.

dataObjects.name: Rate sample
dataObjects.purpose: Keeps the latest cumulative network-received counter, its sample time, and the counter at which the service loop started, so the rate and the total received since the module started can be computed.
dataObjects.retentionIntent: A single record is kept and replaced on each refresh; when the stored sample time is more than twice the refresh interval old, the refresh starts a new baseline at the new reading.

qualityRequirements: The label shows the rate scaled to kB/s with exactly 1 decimal, rounded half away from zero.
The notification total uses the largest SI unit whose value is at least 1, with 2 decimals, and plain B below 1000.
The cache is written as soon as a refresh succeeds; the bar shows it at its next fragment re-run.
productConstraints: The module refreshes the measurement every 2 seconds.
The module command with no action or --once never measures and only re-reads the cached label.
The total received is measured since the service loop started and is not reset by calendar day changes.
